name: avimetaedit
desc: Tool for embedding, validating, and exporting of AVI files metadata
why: Lets you inspect and edit AVI container metadata, a useful look inside an old file format.

brief.what_it_is: AVI MetaEdit is a command-line and GUI-style tool for reading, embedding, validating, and exporting metadata inside AVI video files, covering both Standard AVI and OpenDML variants. It takes an AVI file as input and can write metadata back into it or export that metadata out. It can also check files against file-structure and metadata recommendations from the U.S. National Archives, Microsoft, and IBM. The homepage describes it as an open-source tool that is distributed as binaries for many platforms.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage frames it as a preservation tool: it was initially funded by NARA (National Archives and Records Administration) through the FADGI, designed and led by AVPreserve, and developed by MediaArea. The aim is to make AVI metadata correct and standards-conformant for archival use.
brief.how_it_works: The README says the tool can embed, edit, import, and export metadata in AVI files. The homepage says it can enforce file structure and metadata recommendations and specifications from NARA, Microsoft, and IBM. Its documentation covers views and reports (TECH, CORE, TRACE), error and warning explanations, LIST-INFO and IMIT metadata definitions, XML chunks, audio/video-only checksums, and validation rules. I did not read those documentation pages, so I cannot describe the internals further.
brief.install_notes: The brew formula installs the executable named avimetaedit. The homepage says MediaArea provides binaries for Windows, macOS, Debian, Ubuntu, Linux Mint, RHEL, CentOS, Fedora, openSUSE, ArchLinux, and Flatpak, plus an 'other systems' option. No accounts, runtimes, or first-run configuration appeared in the pages I read.
brief.standout: It does more than read metadata: it checks AVI files against named archival specifications from NARA, Microsoft, and IBM, which is unusual for a container-level tool. Its origin as a federally funded preservation project also makes it an interesting look at how archives define 'correct' AVI metadata.
brief.status: Maintained, with some uncertainty. The homepage lists Version 1.0.2 and links to a ChangeLog and snapshots, and MediaArea hosts the project. I could not find a release date or last-commit date in the pages I read, so I cannot confirm recent activity. The GitHub README I read is short and contains no status note.
brief.caveats: The README contains no command examples, so commands_seen is empty and usage must be taken from the docs, which I did not open. The GitHub README I fetched is short and points to a separate usnationalarchives/AVI-MetaEdit repository for the licence and issues. The homepage asks visitors to donate to support development. Licensing is a mix: the README says the project is public domain in the United States with copyright waived worldwide under CC0 1.0, and the homepage says the code developed by MediaArea is CC0 1.0. The brew caveats field is empty. The scope is AVI only.
quotes: AVI MetaEdit is a tool that supports embedding, validating, and exporting of metadata in AVI (Standard and OpenDML) files.
This tool can also enforce file structure and metadata recommendations and specifications from U.S. National Archives, Microsoft, and IBM.
You can use the tool to embed, edit, import, and export metadata.
